physicians.name: Dr. Camille Ardouin
physicians.shortBio: Sees a small list, one patient at a time, and does every injection herself.

services.name: Consultation
services.shortDescription: An hour, unhurried, with no obligation to book anything afterwards.

services.name: Skin health programme
services.shortDescription: Prescription topicals reviewed every three months.

brand.tone: Quiet, exact, physician-led. Nothing shouted, nothing promised.
brand.photography: Low light, close, texture over faces. Rooms and hands rather than portraits.

concept.thesis: One physician, one room, one list.
concept.positioning: A single-physician cosmetic practice competing with medspas on their terms — price grids and menus — when its actual advantage is that a dermatologist does the work.
knownProblems: The home page opens with a price list, which is the one thing that puts this practice on the same footing as a medspa.
The physician appears once, in a paragraph, below eight treatment tiles.
Every photograph on the site is stock, and it shows.
There is no way to tell, from the site, that a dermatologist performs the treatments personally.
proposedImprovements: Open with the physician, not the menu.
Treatments presented one at a time, at size, with real photography.
An enquiry that reads like the beginning of a conversation rather than a checkout.
Say plainly who holds the syringe.
outOfScope: No before-and-after imagery, in this concept or any other; it is a regulatory and consent question, not a design one.
No pricing, until the practice decides what it wants published.

findings.text: The practice lists one physician and eight treatments.
The home page's first screen is a three-column price grid.
The imagery is licensed stock; the same portrait appears on two unrelated practice sites.
The single-physician model is the differentiator worth leading on — needs confirming that she does in fact perform every treatment before the concept says so.
Proposed hero line: “One physician. One room. Everything done by the person you booked.”
